GPU CLOUD PRICING CALCULATOR · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER

What will your GPU workload cost on each GPU cloud, and when is it cheaper to buy the card?

Pick a GPU, enter the busy GPU-hours per month and how much of the rented time the GPU is really busy. Get RunPod, Lambda, Vast.ai, CoreWeave, AWS, Google Cloud and Modal priced side by side, the 12-month spend, and the hours a month above which owning the card wins — before you leave an H100 idling on a bill.

Nothing is uploaded. Calculated in this browser from numbers you enter and approximate list prices you can edit. It cannot see your cloud account or your invoice.

1. Your workload

2. Comparison

ProviderUSD per GPU-hourPer monthPer year12-month spend with growth

Rent or buy?

Owning = card plus host overhead, depreciated after resale value over your horizon, plus electricity at busy hours. It ignores your time, cooling, noise, failures and idle power.

Rate cards (editable)

ProviderUSD per GPU-hourStorage per GB-month

Owning the card

Press Compare after changing a value. A blank rate means the provider does not offer that GPU. Interruption overhead and per-second billing stay at their defaults here; use the CLI --prices file to edit them.

Prefer a CLI, or want a budget gate in CI?

node cli.mjs compare --gpu h100 --hours 200 --utilization 60 --growth 5
node cli.mjs compare --gpu a100 --gpus 4 --hours 300 --provider aws --budget 2000   # exit 1 over budget
node cli.mjs compare --gpu rtx4090 --hours 120 --prices prices.json --json
node cli.mjs providers

Get cli.mjs and engine.mjs — Node 18+, nothing to install, no network call. More: should I rent or buy a GPU?

Common questions

Does this read my cloud account?

No. It uses only the GPU, GPU-hours, utilisation and storage you type and rate cards you can edit. It cannot see your instances, quotas or invoice. Treat every figure as a way to compare options, never as what you will be charged.

Where do the prices come from?

They are approximate on-demand list prices per GPU-hour as best known in 2025, shown with an as-of line, and every number is editable. GPU rental prices move quickly and vary by region and availability, so check each pricing page before deciding.

What is not included?

Spot or reserved discounts, committed-use contracts, egress, multi-GPU instance shapes that force you to rent more GPUs than you use, regions, support plans and queue or cold-start time. Interruptible capacity is modelled only as a percentage of re-run hours. Use this to compare the hourly lines, not to forecast the whole invoice.

When does buying a GPU beat renting one?

When your busy hours a month pass the breakeven shown: depreciation of the card and host over your horizon, divided by what each busy hour saves against the cheapest rental after electricity. Below it, renting is cheaper; above it, owning is. It ignores your time, noise, cooling, failures and resale uncertainty.

Is my data uploaded anywhere?

No. The page calculates in your browser and sends nothing. The CLI reads local files and makes no network call.

No warranty. This tool is provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied. It is not financial, legal or engineering advice. It multiplies GPU-hours by list prices that may be out of date and ignores spot and reserved pricing, egress, regions, instance shapes and contracts; it is not a quote and not a guarantee of what any vendor will charge. Product names belong to their owners; this project is not affiliated with any of them.

Best-effort hosting, no SLA. These tools are free, experimental, and may be slow, broken, moved, or taken offline without notice. We do not promise uptime, backups of anything you type, or that a URL will keep working. Do not use this as a system of record. If a tool needs to survive, get cli.mjs and run it yourself.

Everything runs in your browser. What you enter is never uploaded; there are no accounts, cookies, or analytics vendors. Anonymous feature events (compare_run, example_loaded) are counted only in local storage and can be deleted with the button below. Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control are honoured.

should-i-rent-or-buy-a-gpu.html.text:
← GPU Training Pricing Calculator

Should I rent or buy a GPU?

Put your GPU, busy hours a month and utilisation into the calculator to price RunPod, Lambda, Vast.ai, CoreWeave, AWS, Google Cloud and Modal side by side and see the buy-versus-rent breakeven. These are the questions to settle before you trust the answer.

When is it cheaper to buy a GPU than to rent one?

When your busy hours a month stay above a breakeven that is usually well under half of a month for consumer cards. Divide the card and host cost, less resale value, by the months you will keep it, then divide by what each busy hour saves against the cheapest rental after electricity. A 24 GB RTX 4090 against a roughly $0.69 an hour rental breaks even at around 70 busy hours a month with the calculator's defaults; an H100 needs far more because rental prices are lower relative to the card. Below breakeven rent; above it, own.

Why is the cheap hourly rate often not the cheap bill?

Instances bill while they are up, not while the GPU is busy. If you launch a pod, run for an hour, and leave it up for two, you paid for two. Enter your real utilisation: at 50% every hourly rate effectively doubles, and a per-second serverless provider with a higher rate can win. Interruptible marketplace capacity adds re-run hours when work is reclaimed.

What should I check before moving a workload?

Whether the GPU you need is offered where you can get capacity, how fast an instance starts and whether your data and checkpoints sit on persistent storage that is billed even when the GPU is off, and whether egress or minimum commitments apply. Run the calculator with your own hours, utilisation and storage, then confirm against each provider's pricing page.

No warranty. This page is provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind. It is not financial or engineering advice; verify prices at each vendor. Best-effort hosting, no SLA.

Support is optional.
